findings.body: The skill drafts and sends the sign-off email before the strict review, so the customer is asked to approve a version that has not passed review. The required order is review, then email for the reviewed version, then reply. In unchanged `src/forge/records.py:267-289`, `forge decision accept` requires approval details before running the review, and line 300 accepts immediately afterward. The revised test at `tests/test_aha_demo.py:40-64` enforces the opposite order from Done-when 6.
findings.title: Not done: Sign-off is read back and drafted

findings.body: The supplied final `Functional check:` paragraph says it ran `forge sync` and read the skill, but its likely-failure sentence only predicts how `forge decision accept` refuses a non-Forge branch. It does not say that command was run or give an observed refusal with a plain next step. The required likely-failure exercise is therefore absent from the check for this revised sign-off flow.

findings.body: All three new item 4–6 tests use `_synced(repo)` here. That helper calls only `forge sync` on an existing fix branch (`tests/test_aha_prepare.py:13-25`). The story's Notes at `plans/FORGE-AHA-1.md:96-98` require checking each instruction through both `forge sync` and `forge init`; no test reads this guidance from a freshly initialized client. Add an init-path assertion for the two host skills.

findings.body: An answer sourced from `agent` or `our default` for one of the first seven topics is still open for sign-off, but `forge next` does not list it: unchanged `src/forge/nextstep.py:106-111` lists only missing, malformed, `ask the client`, or `later` entries. `forge decision accept` rejects those sources separately at `src/forge/records.py:277-285`. An agent relying on this instruction can send the sign-off email before settling such a topic in the read-back call.
findings.title: Correct the claim that forge next lists every open must-answer topic
